transcript:
Agent: Thank you for calling Card Services. My name is Marcus. May I have your name, please?
Customer: Hi Marcus, yes, this is Desmond Achebe.
Agent: Hello Mr. Achebe. Before we begin, could you confirm your billing zip code and the last four digits of your card?
Customer: Sure, the zip code is 30318, and the last four numbers are 4821.
Agent: Thank you. What can I look into for you today?
Customer: Well, I was looking through my recent transactions online and saw a charge for $349.99 that completely surprised me.
Agent: I can help you check that. Do you have the date and the name of the business listed beside the charge?
Customer: Yes, it is from October 1st, and the name says QPX*NOVALINE 8842.
Agent: Got it, October 1st for $349.99 from QPX*NOVALINE 8842. Do you recall buying anything around that date for that amount?
Customer: No, not at all. I have never heard of that place in my life, and I certainly never shopped there.
Agent: Okay. Is there anyone else in your household who might have had permission to use your card?
Customer: No, I live alone. Nobody else has my card or my account information.
Agent: Do you currently have the physical card in your possession?
Customer: Yes, I do. It’s sitting right here in my wallet, exactly where it always is.
Agent: Could this possibly be an annual subscription or a recurring fee that renewed under a parent company name?
Customer: I don't have any subscriptions that cost $349.99. I really have no connection to this company.
Agent: All right, Mr. Achebe. So to make sure I have the full picture, you see a charge on October 1st for $349.99 from QPX*NOVALINE 8842, you have never done business with them, no one else has access to the account, and the physical card is still with you.
Customer: Yes, that is exactly right.
